title.en: Field query Geometric nearest sample on any matching planar arrays

summary: Choose the flattened sample with minimum Euclidean distance; exact ties keep the first sample

capability: Choose the flattened sample with minimum Euclidean distance to each query point; exact ties keep the first sample.
operation: matched planar sample arrays, field values and query points -> sampled field values
discovery.model: Geometric nearest-neighbor selection in matched planar coordinates; no interpolation.
discovery.geometry: Planar matched sample points with x column and y row coordinates, or matched scattered arrays; queries are ordered coordinate pairs.
discovery.boundary: No out-of-support interpolation is synthesized; finite matched samples and queries inside the convex/interpolation support are required, and equivalence with the rectangular scheme on irregular grids is not asserted.

identity.relation: Field query Geometric nearest sample on any matching planar arrays
identity.definition: Choose the flattened sample with minimum Euclidean distance; exact ties keep the first sample. Floating coordinates exactly representable as binary64 use outward-rounded squared-distance intervals: bound the absolute difference, each square and the sum by adjacent floats, with lower bounds clipped at zero. Retain lower <= min(upper), then compare every remaining candidate with exact rational squared distances. Integer and real numeric object coordinates always bypass the floating filter; wider floating formats and queries without exact binary64 conversion also use direct exact comparison.
identity.model: Geometric nearest sample on any matching planar arrays
identity.coordinates: X column coordinate, Y row coordinate or matched scattered point arrays
identity.boundary: Nearest-sample selection only; physical support is the caller's responsibility, with no sorting or domain-membership rejection
assumptions: Finite matched real planar sample coordinates and numeric fields
Requested grid/query points lie inside convex/interpolation support

inputs.name: X
inputs.constraints: Real; for rectangular nearest X[0,:] is x axis

inputs.name: Y
inputs.constraints: Real; for rectangular nearest Y[:,0] is y axis

inputs.name: Q
inputs.description: Finite numeric field samples; selected element types are retained

inputs.name: coord_list
inputs.constraints: Finite real queries; each pair is independently copied and checked as the iterable is consumed once

outputs.name: values
outputs.description: Selected np.asarray(Q).ravel() samples in query order
outputs.constraints: Selected element types are retained; no uniform float64 conversion is applied

preconditions: Finite matched real planar sample coordinates and numeric fields
Requested grid/query points lie inside convex/interpolation support
supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions
excluded: Rectangular and geometric nearest schemes are not asserted equivalent on irregular input
Physical interpretation outside caller-declared support is unqualified; nonfinite field values are rejected

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Nonfinite sample coordinates, Q data or query coordinates reject the whole request with ValueError. Complex sample or query coordinate representations, including zero imaginary parts and complex object elements, also raise ValueError, even when the query batch is empty. Finite complex Q values remain supported. Other conversion, indexing or arithmetic errors propagate. The implementation does not reject unsorted or outside-support queries; the caller determines physical support. Finite numeric object elements are checked without float64 narrowing; real coordinates are compared using their represented numeric values. Unsupported numeric representations still propagate conversion or arithmetic errors.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

example.description: Query the value at the geometrically nearest point in a matched planar sample.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import locs_to_vals1D

x, y = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], [0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
values = locs_to_vals1D(x, y, x + 2.0 * y, [(0.5, 0.5)])
np.testing.assert_allclose(values, [1.5])

The direct regression fixtures listed in verification.tests
The executable example stored in this contract
Analytic unique-nearest fixtures at uniform coordinate scales 1, 1e155 and 1e-170, with an independent hypot reference

Independent 2200-digit Decimal squared-distance references for finite subtraction overflow, rounded distance collisions, subnormal coordinates and true ties; matching shapes, integer precision and real numeric object regressions

Executable interval-enclosure and all-minimizer retention checks against exact rational distances, including subtraction, square and sum overflow, subnormal underflow and ties; the conditional inclusion argument is in the interval helper

Complex coordinate rejection for sample/query arrays and object elements, empty-query validation, finite complex Q preservation, norm-library independence, and direct exact paths for nonfloat or inexact conversions
verification.evidence_ceiling: The candidate-containment argument assumes correctly rounded IEEE binary64 subtraction, multiplication and addition with gradual underflow, exact conversion of filtered inputs and adjacent-float nextafter semantics. It follows from 0 <= lower[i] <= d[i] <= upper[i] and lower[k] <= d[k] <= d[j] <= upper[j] for every true minimizer k and every j; it does not require an error bound for hypot. Named analytic, independent hypot, high-precision Decimal and exact-rational regressions exercise the represented inputs; they do not verify every platform or numeric representation, experimental validity or release approval. Input precision lost before the call cannot be recovered.
known_limitations: Rectangular and geometric nearest schemes are not asserted equivalent on irregular input
Physical interpretation outside caller-declared support is unqualified; nonfinite field values are rejected
